submitted.rationale: Index 8 (Ag 0.55) had the highest measured EQE, 0.893%. It sits just Ag-rich of the AgSbO3 composition, which MACE puts on the hull (the literature gap of about 2.6 eV means it absorbs 2.7 eV light). Index 9 (1:1) gave 0.867% and index 11 (Ag 0.43) gave 0.405%, so EQE peaks at or just Ag-rich of 1:1.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.405% EQE. Performance drops on the Sb-rich side, likely from Ag-deficient or Sb-oxide phases.
Not measured. MEGNet predicts a near-zero gap for Ag3SbO4 and the Ag oxides are likely metallic or unstable, so these compositions were unlikely to beat the AgSbO3 region.

consultations.verdict: MACE says AgSbO3 (mp-540872) is on the hull (0.0002 eV/atom), so the phase should form near Ag:Sb = 1:1. MEGNet's HSE gaps (0.63, 0.43 and 0.09 eV) are well below the experimental ~2.6 eV gap of pyrochlore AgSbO3. I treat MEGNet as underestimating the gap for Ag(I) compounds, so the gap result is uninformative. Stability supports measuring near 50:50 (index 9), where the stable, visibly absorbing AgSbO3 phase is expected.

MACE puts Ag7Sb9O25 (Ag 0.438, a pyrochlore-like Ag-deficient phase) only 0.039 eV/atom above the hull. So Ag-deficient pyrochlore is plausible near index 11 (Ag 0.426), and this supports probing the slightly Sb-rich side of the 1:1 point that gave 0.87%.

MACE puts Ag3SbO4 0.017 eV/atom above the hull, and MEGNet gives it a very small gap (0.09 eV). That argues against going far toward the Ag-rich end, which likely has metallic Ag or Ag3SbO4. EQE fell on the Sb-rich side (0.41% at index 11 vs 0.87% at index 9), so the peak is probably at or just Ag-rich of 1:1. Index 8 (Ag 0.55) is a small, supported step into that region.
